contexts.text: Truth without good... the more it recedes from good, the more it infatuates the man.
Infatuated salt () = truth without any longing for good. AC 9207:4.
Infatuated salt = longing from proprium, thus from the love of self and of the world. Such a longing is infatuated salt, not fit for anything.
Then thick darkness ensues there, and thence infatuation and blindness.
The proprium of man, from which intelligence is infatuated.
The quality of those who are infatuated from Own intelligence...
The love of the will infatuates with falsities the higher things of his understanding.
A scorpion = what is persuasive infatuating and suffocating.

The reason this Persuasive is said to be infatuating, is that it takes away the use of reason... for it excites in a moment everything which consents, and covers over everything which dissents; whence the mind is infatuated by this, that it is in thick darkness...
Hence the speech (of the sensuous man)... fascinates and infatuates the minds of others...
The falsities which are thence, are signified by, They are together infatuated and foolish ().
